subject: Banking
title: How the Fed Is Structured
description: A micro-lesson that makes How the Fed Is Structured usable.

hook.text: The Fed isn't one bank. It's 12 regional reserve banks plus a Board of Governors in Washington.

buildup.text: The Board of Governors has 7 members appointed by the president.

discovery.text: The FOMC, which sets rates, has 12 voting members: all 7 governors plus 5 rotating reserve bank presidents.

twist.text: Regional reserve banks are technically private. Their boards include commercial bankers.

climax.text: The Fed is half public, half private, and entirely powerful.

punchline.text: 12 banks, 7 governors, one rate. The Fed was built on compromise.

quiz.question: How many regional reserve banks make up the Federal Reserve System?
